•A player who has a condition that was treated in the warm-up may take an additional medical timeout for that condition during the match
Toilet/change of attire breaks A tournament may limit the number of breaks if this is announced in advance of the event. The player has a reasonable amount of time for the break. Toilet breaks are allowed only if an official decides that the need is genuine and not because of general fatigue. Play continues if the request is not granted.

title: There is no penalty for receiving an injection, IV infusion, or supplemental oxygen during a suspension of play in which the Referee allows
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.F. Medical Timeout and Bleeding Timeout
text: FAC Comment III.F-2: There is no penalty for receiving an injection, IV infusion, or supplemental oxygen during a suspension of play in which the Referee allows the players to leave the playing area.

title: Request for medical timeout
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.F. Medical Timeout and Bleeding Timeout
text: Request for medical timeout. A request for a medical timeout may be made by a player to the Referee, Chair Umpire, or other official at any time during the match or warm-up.

title: If a player has two medical conditions for which the player requests two medical timeouts, the player should make both requests at the same
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.F. Medical Timeout and Bleeding Timeout
text: FAC Comment III.F-3: If a player has two medical conditions for which the player requests two medical timeouts, the player should make both requests at the same time. The maximum time that play may be interrupted for evaluation and treatment of the two conditions is 15 minutes.

title: Leaving playing area
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.F. Medical Timeout and Bleeding Timeout
text: Leaving playing area. A player requesting a medical timeout or bleeding timeout may leave the playing area to contact the Referee, the Deputy Referee, or other official in charge of the match. If an official is present, the player may not leave the playing area without the official’s permission.

title: Coaching not permitted
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.F. Medical Timeout and Bleeding Timeout
text: Coaching not permitted. No coaching shall be permitted during the suspension of play for a medical timeout or bleeding timeout.

title: Toilet/Change of Attire Breaks
crumb: USTA Regulations · III. Conducting the Tournament
text: A toilet/change of attire break consists of a reasonable amount of time when an official determines that there is genuine need. No coaching is allowed during a toilet/change of attire break.

title: When possible, these breaks should be taken during a set break
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.G. Toilet/Change of Attire Breaks
text: FAC Comment III.G-1: When possible, these breaks should be taken during a set break. If this is not possible, then the break should be taken at an odd game changeover. Breaks taken at other times should be limited to true emergencies.

title: Gastrointestinal problems are medical problems that are governed by medical timeout provisions and not by the toilet break provisions
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.G. Toilet/Change of Attire Breaks
text: FAC Comment III.G-2: Gastrointestinal problems are medical problems that are governed by medical timeout provisions and not by the toilet break provisions.

title: Special Provisions for Wheelchair Tennis Players
crumb: USTA Regulations · III. Conducting the Tournament
text: These provisions apply to wheelchair tennis players regardless of whether they are playing in a Wheelchair Division or another division.

title: Wheelchair repair timeout
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.H. Special Provisions for Wheelchair Tennis Players
text: Wheelchair repair timeout. A player or team may take one or more timeouts for wheelchair repairs during a match. The timeout begins when work begins on the wheelchair and does not include time to locate and bring tools or parts to the court. Any cumulative stoppage of play exceeding 15 minutes will result in the loss of a point; any cumulative stoppage of play exceeding 20 minutes will result in a default (see Table 15). Any time taken within a 90-second changeover and a 120-second set break to repair a wheelchair does not count toward the cumulative time permitted for a wheelchair repair timeout. If play resumes after 15 minutes, but before a default, the players are entitled to a re-warm-up of the same duration as the original warm-up. No coaching is allowed during a wheelchair repair timeout.

title: Re-strapping racket by Quad wheelchair player on changeover or set break
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.H. Special Provisions for Wheelchair Tennis Players
text:
Re-strapping racket by Quad wheelchair player on changeover or set break. When an official determines that there is genuine need, a
reasonable amount of time may be given to a Quad wheelchair player during a changeover or a set break to re-strap the racket to their hand without incurring a penalty. No coaching is allowed during re-strapping.

title: Shortening Tournaments
crumb: USTA Regulations · III. Conducting the Tournament
text:
Inclement weather, health concerns, or safety concerns may require the
Referee to take steps to shorten the tournament to keep the tournament on schedule, including, but not limited to:

title: Switch to No-Ad scoring
text: Switch to No-Ad scoring. The Referee may switch to No-Ad scoring for any complete round, except that the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations may limit the use of No-Ad scoring at USTA National Junior Tournaments.

title: Switch to Match Tiebreak in lieu of deciding final set, short sets, or pro sets
text: Switch to Match Tiebreak in lieu of deciding final set, short sets, or pro sets. The Referee may switch to a Match Tiebreak in lieu of a deciding final set, short sets, or pro sets for any complete round, except that, the USTA Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations for the respective divisions may limit the use of this format when this format may be used in national tournaments.

title: Strictly enforce pre-match warm-up time and breaks between sets
text: Strictly enforce pre-match warm-up time and breaks between sets.

title: Tighten court usage
text: Tighten court usage. Use “to be followed by” scheduling and have players waiting at courtside as soon as matches finish.

title: Cancel matches
text:
Cancel matches.
a. Junior Divisions. Referees are encouraged to cancel matches in the following order:
• consolation doubles;
• consolation singles;
• main draw doubles; and
• main draw singles. The USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations specify when this order of canceling matches is mandatory in USTA National Junior Tournaments.
b. Other divisions. If some matches in a division must be canceled, start with consolation rounds. Cancel main draw singles matches last. If there is no practical way to finish an event, the Tournament Committee shall either make arrangements that are mutually agreeable to the players to finish at a later date, or in the absence of such arrangements, declare the tournament event unfinished.

title: The Referee should cancel matches on a division-bydivision basis and should try to avoid a situation in which some, but not all, matches in
text: FAC Comment III.I-1: The Referee should cancel matches on a division-bydivision basis and should try to avoid a situation in which some, but not all, matches in a round in a division are completed.

title: What does a Referee do if a tournament event cannot be finished without violating some of the scheduling guidelines?
text:
FAC Comment III.I-2: What does a Referee do if a tournament event cannot be finished without violating some of the scheduling guidelines? First, the Referee may not violate the minimum rest between matches in Table 11. Second, the Referee should remember that the principle behind these guidelines is the protection of the health of the players. Third, the Referee should keep to a minimum the number of situations in which the guidelines in USTA Regulation II.D.9. and Tables 8 and 9 are not followed. For example, it makes sense to start a 12-and-under match after 8 p.m. if that will prevent several players from having
to play three singles matches the following day. This situation might also mean that the Referee may have to delay the start of the next morning’s matches in order to give a player enough sleep over night. In short, the Referee has to use judgment, keeping in mind the principle of the health of the players.

title: Ball-change errors
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.J. Ball-Change Errors, Ball Replacement, and Practice Balls
text: Ball-change errors. Ball-change errors are handled under Rule 27i of the ITF Rules of Tennis.

title: Balls that become unfit for play
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.J. Ball-Change Errors, Ball Replacement, and Practice Balls
text: Balls that become unfit for play. If a ball becomes unfit for play (for example, ball breaks or loses compression), it shall be replaced immediately. If a ball becomes wet, it may be taken out of play temporarily until it dries, or it may be replaced.

title: Replacement of balls
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.J. Ball-Change Errors, Ball Replacement, and Practice Balls
text: Replacement of balls. If a ball has to be replaced during the warm-up or before the start of the third game after a ball change, the ball shall be replaced with a new ball. At all other times it shall be replaced with a ball of like wear to the remaining balls.

title: Resuming play after suspension of match
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.J. Ball-Change Errors, Ball Replacement, and Practice Balls
text: Resuming play after suspension of match. In matches where a ball change is authorized only at the start of the third set, warm-up after a suspension may be conducted with the match balls. In all other matches, warm-ups after a suspension should be conducted with balls other than the match balls. If other balls are not available, then the match balls may be used, but the balls should be changed two games sooner than the originally specified number of games. When an Umpire or Referee determines that the condition of the balls has materially changed since suspension of play, the match shall be resumed with balls whose condition is equivalent to the condition of the balls that were being used before their condition materially changed. If this is not possible, the match shall be resumed with new balls and re-warm-up shall be conducted with the new balls.

title: Practice during rest period
crumb: USTA Regulations · III.J. Ball-Change Errors, Ball Replacement, and Practice Balls
text: Practice during rest period. Except in junior divisions, the Referee may permit practice on the match court during a rest period, but not with the match balls.

title: USTA membership verification
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.A. Checking in at Tournament
text: USTA membership verification. When USTA membership verification is required, a player must provide the Tournament Committee with verification of current USTA membership. A foreign nonresident player who has proof that the player is a member of the player’s National Association is exempt from this requirement.

title: Check-in at tournament desk
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.A. Checking in at Tournament
text: Check-in at tournament desk. A player shall check in at the tournament desk before the scheduled time of each match. The Referee shall designate a place at which players shall check in. A player is not deemed to have arrived until the player checks in at the designated place and the player is properly clothed, equipped, and ready to play. The Referee may penalize a player who is on site for lateness if a court is available and the player has failed to check in at the tournament desk by the scheduled match time.

title: Obtain time of next match
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.A. Checking in at Tournament
text: Obtain time of next match. The player is responsible for obtaining the time of the player’s matches from the Referee, rather than vice versa. Unless specifically authorized by the Referee, schedules of play carried in newspapers or other media are not official, and a player utilizes them at the player’s own risk.

title: Player Responsibilities Under The Code
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV. Player Responsibilities and Conduct
text: Players shall follow The Code, except to the extent an official assumes some of the players’ responsibilities. The Code is a USTA publication originally written by Col. N.E. Powel. The Code shall apply in all cases not specifically covered by the USTA Regulations.

title: General
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: General. Players, persons who appear to be associated with a player (including, but not limited to, parents and coaches), officials, and organizers of any tournament are under a duty to encourage and maintain high standards of proper conduct, fair play, and good sportsmanship. They are under an obligation to avoid acts that may be considered detrimental to the game of tennis. Detrimental acts include, but are not limited to, the acts in USTA Regulation IV.C. The Chair of any tournament may withhold all or part of any prize money or expenses payable to any player charged by the Chair or by the Referee of the tournament with conduct inconsistent with the principles in USTA Regulation IV.C., provided a written grievance is filed in accordance with USTA Regulation V.B. and Bylaw 43. Any prize money or expenses so withheld shall be withheld until a final d etermination of the charges in the grievance has been made. Immediately after the final determination, the funds withheld, less the amount of any fine, shall be promptly paid to the player.

title: USTA Anti-Doping Program
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text:
USTA Anti-Doping Program. The USTA is committed to ensuring fair and drug-free competition. All athletes shall compete fairly and drug-free. Participation in USTA tournaments constitutes consent to be tested for drugs. All athletes shall comply with all anti-doping rules and all other policies and rules of the World Anti-Doping Agency (“WADA”); the International Tennis Integrity Agency (“ITIA”); the United States Olympic and Paralympic Movement (“USOPC”), including the USOPC National Anti- Doping Policy; and the U.S. Anti-Doping Agency (“USADA”), including the
USADA Protocol for Olympic and Paralympic Movement Testing (“USADA Protocol”). All athletes shall submit to drug testing by the ITIA and/or USADA or their designees at any time and understand that the use of methods or substances prohibited by the applicable anti-doping rules make them subject to penalties including, but not limited to, disqualification, suspension, and revocation of membership. If it is determined that an athlete may have committed a doping violation, the athlete agrees to submit to the results management authority and processes of USADA, including arbitration under the USADA Protocol, or to the results management authority of the ITIA and/ or USTA, if applicable or referred by USADA.

title: Shoes
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Shoes. A player may not wear shoes that mar or damage the court.

title: Warm-up
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Warm-up. A player who refuses to warm-up with the opponent forfeits the right to a warm-up. During the warm-up or a re-warm-up, a player may have any person hit with the player if the opponent refuses to do so.

title: Leaving playing area
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct

title: Leaving tournament area after match is suspended
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Leaving tournament area after match is suspended. When a match has been suspended, a player may not leave the tournament area until the player has obtained from the Referee either the time the player is next to play or clearance to leave.

title: Practice during rest period
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Practice during rest period. During a rest period in all divisions other than juniors, the Referee may permit practice on the match court. In Junior Divisions, no player may practice on any court during a rest period. Practice with the match balls shall never be permitted.

title: Removal of official
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Removal of official. A player is not entitled to have an official removed from a match.

title: Inspection of ball marks
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Inspection of ball marks. A player shall not pass the net to inspect a ball mark.

title: No coaching
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text:
No coaching. Except as permitted under Rule 30 of the ITF Rules of Tennis, a player may not receive coaching during any suspension or interruption of play due to the following:
a. Medical timeout or bleeding timeout under USTA Regulations III.F.1 and III.F.2.;
b. Maladjustment of a player’s clothing, footwear, or equipment under Rule 29.b of the ITF Rules of Tennis;
c. Toilet/change of attire break under Rule 29.c of the ITF Rules of Tennis and USTA Regulation III.G.; or
d. Wheelchair repair timeout or additional time for a Quad wheelchair player to re-strap a racket under USTA Regulation III.H.; or
e. Seeking the assistance of an official under USTA Regulation IV.C.5.
Coaching is permitted during a rest period between sets under Rule 30 of the ITF Rules of Tennis and during any other suspension of play under either USTA Regulation III.E. or Rule 30. A temporary interruption of play during which the players do not leave the playing area is not a “suspension” of play for these purposes. Coaching is not permitted during any warm-up.

title: Unsportsmanlike conduct by player or person associated with player
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Unsportsmanlike conduct by player or person associated with player. A player who enters a sanctioned tournament or match consents to being penalized under the Point Penalty System and the USTA Suspension Point System for any unsportsmanlike conduct, including conduct by a person associated with the player. Persons who are unsportsmanlike may be asked by any member of the Tournament Committee or any official representative of the tournament to desist and/or to leave the tournament site, and must comply.

title: Player shall not enter two tournaments at same time
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Player shall not enter two tournaments at same time. When entries close, a player shall not be entered in two or more sanctioned tournaments, if any part of the tournaments overlap unless each Tournament Committee involved understands the situation and concurs in writing. After a player has been eliminated from a tournament whose schedule of play partially overlaps with that of a second tournament, the player may enter the second tournament. This restriction may be waived by the USTA or one of its Sectional or District Associations.

title: Player shall not enter tournament intending to withdraw if player’s entry is accepted in another tournament
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Player shall not enter tournament intending to withdraw if player’s entry is accepted in another tournament. A player shall not enter a tournament with the intention of withdrawing if the player’s entry is accepted in another tournament, unless the Tournament Committee for the tournament in which the player has entered understands the situation and concurs with the contemplated action. This restriction may be waived by the USTA or one of its Sectional or District Associations.

title: Player shall not enter tournament player cannot finish
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Player shall not enter tournament player cannot finish. Player shall not enter a tournament (including mandatory consolation) knowing the player will be unable to finish.

title: Player shall not transfer entry
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Player shall not transfer entry. Player shall not transfer entry in a tournament to another player.

title: Player shall not withdraw from tournament after entries close except for illness, injury, personal circumstance, or previously authorized en
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text:
Player shall not withdraw from tournament after entries close except for illness, injury, personal circumstance, or previously authorized entry into another tournament. A player shall not withdraw from a tournament after entries close except for illness, injury, personal circumstance, or previously authorized entry into another tournament. If the player withdraws for other reasons after the draw has been made and the player has not been replaced with another player, the match shall be recorded as a default. A withdrawing player shall immediately notify the Tournament Committee or Referee by telephone, electronic communication, or in person that the player will not be playing.
• If the player is not playing b ecause of an injury or illness, the player shall deliver written verification of the injury or illness from a medical professional to the Referee no later than the last scheduled day of the tournament.
• If the player is not playing because of a personal circumstance,
the player shall deliver a written description of the situation to the Referee no later than the last scheduled day of the tournament. The Referee shall determine whether the situation is a personal circumstance. The Tournament Committee may waive these requirements unless prohibited from doing so by applicable National, sectional, or district regulations, or the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations.

title: Player shall not fail to appear for reasons other than injury, illness, or personal circumstance
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Player shall not fail to appear for reasons other than injury, illness, or personal circumstance. A player shall not enter a tournament and then fail to appear for a match (whether in the qualifying, main, or consolation draw) except for illness, injury, or personal circumstance. If the player’s reason for failing to appear is not one of these reasons, or if the player gives no reason for failing to appear, then the match shall be recorded as a default.

title: A player entered in a tournament who withdraws before the draw is made or who withdraws after the draw is made, but is replaced with an alte
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: FAC Comment IV.C-2: A player entered in a tournament who withdraws before the draw is made or who withdraws after the draw is made, but is replaced with an alternate, and the reason for the withdrawal is not for injury, illness, personal circumstance, or previously authorized entry into another tournament, is subject to the USTA Suspension Point System. (See Table 17.)

title: Player shall not engage in unsportsmanlike conduct
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct

title: Player shall not engage in gambling activity
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct

title: Point Penalty System
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.C. Standards of Conduct
text: Point Penalty System. A player shall not engage in conduct that calls for a penalty under the Point Penalty System. Any player who v iolates any USTA Tournament Regulation may be penalized under the Point Penalty System.

title: Mandatory use in any sanctioned tournament
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Mandatory use in any sanctioned tournament. The Point Penalty System applies to violations occurring during the warm-up and the match in any sanctioned tournament, except that it does not apply to Net Generation Programs that use Red Ball Tennis and it only applies when authorized by a Sectional Association in Net Generation Programs that use Orange, Green, and Yellow Ball Tennis.

title: Purposes of System
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text:
Purposes of System. The purposes of the System are to:
a. deter unsportsmanlike conduct by a player and persons associated with players;
b. ensure compliance with the continuous play rule; and
c. ensure on-time appearance for matches. The objective of the Point Penalty System is not to punish, but to secure compliance with the ITF Rules of Tennis and USTA Regulations.

title: Code violations for misconduct
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Code violations for misconduct. Misconduct shall be penalized pursuant to Table 14.

title: Time violations
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Time violations. Time violations shall be penalized pursuant to Table 15.

title: Delay between points
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Delay between points. When practical in tournaments using a certified official in direct observation of the match, the time that shall elapse from the moment the ball goes out of play until the ball is struck shall not exceed 25 seconds.

title: Officials authorized to impose penalties
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text:
Officials authorized to impose penalties.
a. Referee. A Referee may impose a penalty only if the Referee has seen or heard enough to be able to determine with reasonable certainty that a violation has occurred. A Referee may also impose a penalty based on the report of what a Court Monitor or official has seen or heard or on an admission from a player whose conduct is in question.
b. Chair Umpire. The Chair Umpire is primarily responsible for imposing penalties in a chaired match. If a Line Umpire observes a conduct violation or is the object of unsportsmanlike conduct by a player, the Line Umpire shall, as soon as possible and without disrupting play, inform the Chair Umpire. The Chair Umpire shall then make a decision under the Point Penalty System.
c. Roving Umpire. Roving Umpires are primarily responsible for imposing penalties in matches without Chair Umpires. Roving Umpires may impose a penalty only if they have seen, heard, or otherwise observed enough to be able to determine with reasonable certainty that a violation has occurred.

title: An official should impose a penalty only when the official is in position to determine what has happened with reasonable certainty
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: FAC Comment IV.D-1: An official should impose a penalty only when the official is in position to determine what has happened with reasonable certainty. While normally this is based on what the official personally saw or heard, the determination could also be based on the report of a Court Monitor or official or an admission from the player whose conduct is in question.

title: Flagrant violations
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Flagrant violations. While the imposition of penalties normally follows the progression of penalties from point to game to default found in Table 14, any flagrantly unsportsmanlike act by a player or person associated with a player may result in immediate default. If an Umpire imposes the default, the player may appeal to the Referee. If the Referee imposes the default, the player may appeal to the Tournament Appeals Committee.

title: Appeal of penalty to Referee
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Appeal of penalty to Referee. A player has the right to appeal a penalty, but the appeal is limited to questions of law. (See Appendix VII (Role of Court Officials) of the ITF Rules of Tennis.)

title: Penalties to be imposed on doubles team
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text:
Penalties to be imposed on doubles team. A penalty on a member of a doubles team is considered to have been imposed on the team for all purposes except that a doubles partner who was not responsible for the penalty:
• Is not penalized under the USTA Suspension Point System;
• Does not lose ranking points for the tournament in junior divisions (See USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations); and
• May play in other events in the tournament (See USTA Regulation III.B.6.).

title: Penalties treated as if points actually played
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Penalties treated as if points actually played. All penalties under the Point Penalty System are treated as though the penalty points or penalty games actually had been played so far as serving order, court occupancy, and ball change are concerned. One exception, as Table 16 indicates, is that a player penalized for lateness also shall be deemed to have lost the toss provided for in Rule 9 of the ITF Rules of Tennis. The penalized player is allowed to choose an option, but only after the opponent has chosen. A second exception is that the first ball change shall be calculated from the first game played. The choice to serve or receive shall apply to the first game played.

title: Time delays when each side is responsible
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Time delays when each side is responsible. If both players or teams are equally responsible for delay during a match, any penalty will be imposed upon the server.

title: Penalties after medical condition develops
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Penalties after medical condition develops. Except during the warm-up, a player suffering from a medical condition may buy time with a penalty.

title: Penalties imposed between games or before match
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Penalties imposed between games or before match. A penalty imposed between games or before the start of a match shall apply to the first point of the next game scheduled to be played.

title: Point penalties
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Point penalties. A point penalty is scored as though the player had played and lost what would have been the next point.

title: Timing of imposition of penalties
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Timing of imposition of penalties. An official who is on the court must impose penalties before the start of the next point. An official who is not on the court has a reasonable amount of time to reach the court and impose the penalty even if intervening points have been played. Any intervening points stand as played.

title: Player may not decline penalty
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Player may not decline penalty. A player who is the beneficiary of a penalty imposed upon the opponent may not decline to accept it. A player who disobeys the instructions of an official in such a case is liable to being defaulted.

title: Reporting penalties to Referee
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Reporting penalties to Referee. When feasible, a Chair Umpire or Roving Umpire should promptly notify the Referee that a code violation has been assessed. After a match, officials shall report to the Referee each code violation imposed.

title: Other disciplinary action
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Other disciplinary action. Nothing in the Point Penalty System rules out a subsequent imposition of monetary fines, suspensions, or other disciplinary actions by whatever governing body has jurisdiction.

title: Announcing score after penalty
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.D. Point Penalty System
text: Announcing score after penalty. After a point or game penalty, the new score should be announced. After assessing a penalty that ends the match, the official should delay announcing the score until the official determines whether the penalized player will appeal.

• Failure to follow the instructions of an official

Time Violations Penalties

title: Default of player for cause
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.E. Defaults and Disqualifications
text: Default of player for cause. The Referee, Deputy Referee, Chair Umpire, or Roving Umpire may default a player. A player may be defaulted for cause including, but not limited to, tardiness or misconduct (which includes failure to follow the instructions of an official).

title: Disqualification of ineligible player
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.E. Defaults and Disqualifications
text: Disqualification of ineligible player. Upon presentation of proof, the Referee shall disqualify a player who has entered a tournament for which the player is ineligible because of age or other restrictions that apply for that tournament. The Referee may reinstate the loser of the last match won by the disqualified player.

title: Appeal to Tournament Appeals Committee of disqualification or u nilateral default issued by Referee
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.E. Defaults and Disqualifications
text:
Appeal to Tournament Appeals Committee of disqualification or u nilateral default issued by Referee. A player who has been disqualified or unilaterally defaulted by the Referee may appeal the decision by notifying the Referee. The Tournament Appeals Committee hears the appeal, and its decision is final. The time in which to appeal is limited.
• If the default was issued when the player was on court, the player must appeal before leaving the playing area.
• If the default was not issued when the player was on court, the player has 15 minutes to appeal from the time that the player learns of the decision.

title: Appeal to Referee of default issued by official other than Referee
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.E. Defaults and Disqualifications
text:
Appeal to Referee of default issued by official other than Referee. A player who has been defaulted by an official other than the Referee may appeal the default to the Referee.
• If the default was issued when the player was on court, the player, before leaving the playing area, must notify the official who issued the default (or the Referee if the Referee was present) that the player wishes to appeal
• If the default was not issued when the player was on court, the player has 15 minutes to appeal from the time that the player learns of the decision. The Referee’s decision shall be final. In the absence of the Referee, a Deputy Referee shall decide the appeal unless it was that Deputy Referee who issued the default, in which case the Tournament Appeals Committee shall decide the appeal.

title: Players shall not leave playing area while appeal is pending
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.E. Defaults and Disqualifications
text: Players shall not leave playing area while appeal is pending. When a player appeals an on-court disqualification or default, the player must appeal before the players leave the playing area. When an appeal has been made, no player shall depart the playing area until the appeal has been acted upon.

title: Betting
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.E. Defaults and Disqualifications
text: Betting. If a player bets on any match, the Referee shall immediately default the player from all events and remove the offender from any further connection with the tournament.

6. Reporting misconduct. Persons who observe misconduct on or off the court should report it to the Referee.
a. Reporting to National Suspension Point administrator. Persons who observe misconduct associated with a tournament sanctioned by the USTA pursuant to USTA Regulation XVII.D., E., and F. may report it to the National Suspension Point administrator.
b. Reporting to applicable Sectional Association or District Association designee. Persons who observe misconduct associated with a tournament sanctioned by a Sectional Association or one of its District Associations, may report it to the applicable Sectional Association or District Association designee. When a Sectional Association’s or District Association’s Grievance Committee is permitted to assess suspension points, the Sectional Association or District Association designee may refer a report to the applicable Grievance Committee.
c. Reporting to applicable Sectional or District Grievance Committee. If permitted by a Sectional Association, misconduct associated with a tournament sanctioned by a Sectional Association or one of its District Associations may be reported to the applicable Grievance Committee, pursuant to the grievance procedures of the applicable Sectional Association or District Association.
7. Assessing suspension points. Any person who assesses suspension points may do so only if the person has seen or heard the violation, or has been presented with enough documentation to determine with reasonable certainty that a violation in Table 17 has occurred.
a. The Referee. The Referee may assess suspension points pursuant to Table 17.
b. The National Suspension Point administrator. The applicable National Suspension Point administrator may assess suspension points pursuant to Table 17.B.6., 17.C., and 17.F. for misconduct associated with tournaments sanctioned by the USTA pursuant to USTA Regulation XVII.D., E. and F. within seven days after the end of the tournament.
c. Sectional or District Association designee. A designee of the sanctioning association may assess suspension points pursuant to Table 17.B.6., 17.C., and 17.F. within seven days after the end of the tournament.
d. Grievance Committee of a Sectional or District Association. If permitted by a Sectional Association, the Grievance Committee of the Sectional Association or District Association may assess suspension points pursuant to Table 17.B.6., 17.C., 17.D.3. and 4., 17.E., and 17.F. 8. Recording suspension points. Suspension points assessed by a Referee shall be recorded within three days after the end of the tournament. All other suspension points shall be recorded within three days after assessment. The recording period does not apply when suspension points are assessed by an association’s Grievance Committee pursuant to USTA Regulation IV.F.7.c. The recording of suspension points assessed is an administrative task and failure to record shall not invalidate any penalties imposed or suspension points assessed.

title: When a violation occurs that involves a doubles team, suspension points shall be assessed only to the doubles player who was responsible for
crumb: USTA Regulations · IV.G. ITF                Each suspension point assessed at ITF tournaments and
text:
FAC Comment IV.F-1: When a violation occurs that involves a doubles team, suspension points shall be assessed only to the doubles player who was responsible for the violation.
9. Notification to player of points assessed. The person filing the suspension point report pursuant to USTA Regulation IV.F.5. or that person’s designee shall notify the player of the suspension points assessed within seven days after the end of the tournament and shall record the method of notification. Failure to notify the player or record the method of notification shall not invalidate any penalties imposed or suspension points assessed.
10. Appeal of suspension points.
a. Suspension points assessed at sectional tournaments. A Sectional
Association, at its discretion, may adopt a procedure for permitting a player to appeal suspension points assessed at tournaments sanctioned by the Sectional Association or one of its District Associations, provided that no person who participated in the assessment of the suspension points may participate in ruling on the appeal. Points removed from a player’s record as a result of an appeal process shall not count toward a suspension.
b. Suspension points assessed at national tournaments. A player may appeal suspension points assessed at national tournaments only after the player has accumulated sufficient points to be suspended.
c. Appeal of suspension points. After the player has accumulated sufficient points to be suspended, all suspension points are appealable.
11. Player suspension. The USTA shall suspend players according to the following schedule:
a. First suspension. If a player receives 10 suspension points within a 12-month period, the player shall be suspended from competing in sanctioned tournaments for three months. (If no USTA National Championship falls during the 3-month period, the player shall not be accepted into the USTA National Championship immediately following the 3-month suspension period.) Upon suspension these 10 points shall be cleared from the player’s record. All other suspension points shall remain on the player’s record and count toward a second suspension.
b. Second suspension. If a player receives 8 suspension points within the 12 months immediately following the first suspension, the player shall be suspended from competing in sanctioned tournaments for 6 months. Upon suspension these 8 points shall be cleared from the player’s record. All other suspension points shall remain on the player’s record and count toward a third suspension.
c. Subsequent suspensions. If a player receives 6 suspension points within the 12-month period immediately following the second suspension (and any suspensions subsequent to the second suspension), the player shall be suspended from competing in sanctioned tournaments for a period to be determined by the applicable National Suspension Point administrator, the chair of the applicable committee, and one additional member of the applicable committee appointed by its chair. The suspension period shall not be less than one year. In the case of a junior player, including a junior wheelchair player, the maximum suspension period is the remainder of the player’s junior career. These 6 points shall be cleared from the player’s record.
12. Written notice of suspension to player and Sectional Association. After the USTA has determined that a player will be suspended, the applicable National Suspension Point administrator shall send a notice by first class mail and by certified mail (return receipt requested) to the player at the address shown on the records of the Membership Department with a copy to the player’s Sectional Association. The notice shall state:
• That the player is being suspended;
• The length of the suspension;
• The player’s right to appeal the suspension under USTA Regulation IV.F.11.;
• The procedure for appealing the suspension; and
• A statement that if the player chooses not to appeal the suspension, then the suspension shall begin 30 days after the date the notice was mailed. Failure of the applicable National Suspension Point administrator to notify a Sectional Association shall not invalidate the suspension.
13. Player may request that suspension start immediately. When a player accumulates sufficient points to be suspended, the player may request that the suspension period begin immediately. The player shall mail the request by certified mail, return receipt requested, to the applicable National Suspension Point administrator. If the applicable National Suspension Point administrator confirms that the player has accumulated sufficient points to be suspended, the suspension shall begin on the date that the certified notice was mailed.
14. Right to appeal suspension.
a. Suspension points at national tournaments and ITF tournaments. When at least one suspension point that results in a suspension is assessed at a tournament sanctioned by the applicable national committee or at an ITF tournament, any appeal shall be filed with the USTA Grievance Committee in accordance with USTA Bylaw 43f.ii. Absent good cause shown, any appeal shall be barred unless it is made in writing within 30 days of mailing the notice of suspension. The notice of appeal shall be mailed first class certified or registered mail to the Grievance Chair, c/o USTA Office of the General Counsel, 2500 Westchester Avenue, Suite 411, Purchase, New York 10577.
b. All suspension points at tournaments sanctioned by one Sectional Association. When all suspension points that result in a suspension are assessed at tournaments sanctioned by one Sectional Association, any appeal shall be filed with the Sectional Association that sanctioned the tournaments. Unless the Sectional Association grievance procedures provide a longer period for appeal or absent good cause shown, any appeal shall be barred unless it is made in writing within 30 days of mailing the notice of suspension. The notice of appeal shall be mailed first class certified or registered mail to the Grievance Chair of the Sectional Association. The Sectional Association shall notify the applicable National Suspension Point administrator of the appeal and whether a stay has been granted. Following the disposition of the appeal, the Sectional Association shall notify the applicable National Suspension Point administrator of the decision on the appeal.
c. Suspension points at tournaments sanctioned by more than one Sectional Association. When suspension points are accumulated at different tournaments sanctioned by different Sectional Associations or District Associations of more than one Sectional Association, the procedure in USTA Regulation IV.F.14.a. applies.
15. Effective date of suspension.
a. If the player does not appeal the suspension, the suspension begins 30 days after the applicable National Suspension Point administrator mails the certified notice of suspension to the player or such earlier date as may be requested in writing by the player under USTA Regulation IV.F.13.
b. If the player appeals the suspension and the appeal is denied, the suspension begins on the date the decision is mailed unless the decision states otherwise or unless a stay is granted.

title: Submit draw sheets to USTA within three days
crumb: USTA Regulations · V.A. Responsibilities of Tournament Committee and Referee After C         ompletion
text: Submit draw sheets to USTA within three days. Within three days after the completion of a tournament, the Tournament Committee shall submit to the body issuing the sanction complete and legible draws containing first and last names of all players, match scores, and other information that is required by the body issuing the sanction. Failure to submit these reports may bring about disciplinary action by the sanctioning body. The foregoing also applies to Feed-In Championships and consolations conducted as part of the tournament.

title: Reports on players whose prize money was withheld
crumb: USTA Regulations · V.A. Responsibilities of Tournament Committee and Referee After C         ompletion
text: Reports on players whose prize money was withheld. Within three days after the completion of a tournament, the Tournament Committee shall file a report with the USTA Grievance Committee on any player whose prize money was withheld pursuant to USTA Regulation IV.C.1. Failure to submit these reports may bring about disciplinary action by the sanctioning body.

title: Referee reports violations of USTA Regulations within three days
crumb: USTA Regulations · V.A. Responsibilities of Tournament Committee and Referee After C         ompletion
text:
Referee reports violations of USTA Regulations within three days. Within three days after the end of a tournament, the Referee shall file a written report of:
• All violations of USTA Regulations and penalties imposed with the Sectional Association where the tournament was held and with the player’s Sectional Association. If the tournament was a tournament published on a national tournament schedule, the Referee also shall file the report with the applicable USTA Competition Department; and
• All suspension points assessed under the USTA Suspension Points System with the USTA. See USTA Regulation IV.F. Failure to file the written report within three days shall not invalidate any post-tournament disciplinary action based on violations of USTA Regulations nor shall it invalidate any penalties imposed or suspension points assessed.

title: Grievances
text:
Any official, volunteer, player, or person associated with a player (including, but not limited to, a parent or coach) who observes a violation of USTA regulations, standards of conduct, fair play, or good sportsmanship may file a written grievance according to the grievance procedures of the Sectional Association where the tournament was held; except if the conduct arises out of any of the following, the grievance must be filed with the Chair of the USTA Grievance Committee, c/o USTA Office of General Counsel, 2500 Westchester Avenue, Suite 411, Purchase, New York 10577:
• Tournaments on a national tournament schedule;
• International competitions in which USTA players participate; or
• Denial of entry into a tournament on the basis of residency. (See USTA Bylaw 43 for procedures and time frames for the filing of grievances and appeals.)

title: Suspensions by Sectional and District Associations
text:
Suspensions from participation in sanctioned tournaments imposed by Sectional Associations or District Associations as the result of a grievance or as a result of a suspension imposed under the USTA Suspension Point
System, shall be enforced in all USTA sanctioned tournaments, whether they are sanctioned by the Sectional or District Association, another Sectional or District Association, or the USTA. The Sectional Association or District Association shall send notice of the suspension to the National Suspension Point administrator. The reporting of suspension points assessed is an administrative task and the failure to report shall not invalidate any suspension.

Fig. 7 Instructions for Laying Out 36-Foot Court on Top of Regulation 78-Foot Court
The Court The court shall be a rectangle that is 36 feet long and 18 feet wide. This size shall be used for singles and doubles.
The Net The court shall be divided across the middle by a net suspended by a cord that shall pass over or be attached to two net posts at a height of 33 inches. The net shall be fully extended so that it completely fills the space between the two net posts and must be made of sufficiently small mesh so that a ball cannot pass through it. The height of the net at its c enter shall be 33 inches.
Marking the Lines on the Court
• Create two baselines by drawing lines that are 36 feet apart at the ends of the court. (This places the baselines on top of the doubles sidelines of a 78-foot court.)
• Create two sidelines by drawing lines that are 18 feet apart and perpendicular to the baselines. They are used for singles and doubles. (This places the sidelines on the baseline and service line of a 78-foot court.)
• Create two service lines by drawing lines between the sidelines that are parallel to each baseline and 4 feet 6 inches inside each baseline.
• Create the center service line by starting at one service line and drawing a line parallel to the sidelines that is halfway between the sidelines and that ends at the other service line. (The center s ervice line results in the formation of two service courts on each side of the court.)
• Divide each baseline in half by a 2-inch wide center mark that is drawn inside the baseline and parallel to the sidelines.
• All lines shall be 1.5 inches wide, the same color, and shall clearly contrast with the color of the surface. If the lines are painted on a 78-foot court, they shall be of a different color than the lines on the 78-foot court and shall stop 3 inches from the standard lines.
• All measurements shall be made to the outside of the lines.

• Create two baselines by drawing lines that are 60 feet apart at the ends of the court.
• Create two singles sidelines by drawing lines that are 27 feet apart and perpendicular to the baselines. Leave a 2-inch gap in each sideline immediately behind each service line.
• Create two doubles sidelines by drawing lines that are 33 feet apart and perpendicular to the baselines. (This places the doubles sidelines on top of the singles sideline for a 78-foot court.)
• Use the existing service lines of the 78-foot court as the service lines.
• Use the existing center service line of the 78-foot court as the center service line.
• Divide each baseline in half by a 2-inch wide center mark that is drawn inside the baseline and parallel to the sidelines.
• All lines shall be 1.5 inches wide, the same color, and shall clearly contrast with the color of the surface. If the baselines and singles sidelines are painted on a 78-foot court, they shall be of a different color than the lines on the 78-foot court.
• All measurements shall be made to the outside of the lines.

title: Safe Play. All officials seeking USTA certification must comply and be
text: current with the requirements of the USTA Safe Play Program, including clearing a criminal background screen and completing SafeSport training (see usta.com/safeplay for more information).

title: Betting
text: No official may gamble (directly or indirectly) on any tennis match. No official may assist any person in gambling on tennis.

title: Purpose
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.C. Certification of USTA Officials
text: Purpose. The USTA certifies officials for officiating at USTA-sanctioned tournaments. USTA certification is an indication of ability, experience, and competence. Certification assists sanction holders in selecting and assigning officials to USTA-sanctioned tournaments. USTA-certified officials adhere to the ITF Rules of Tennis, ITF Duties and Procedures, and USTA regulations.

title: Regulations for certification of officials
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.C. Certification of USTA Officials
text: Regulations for certification of officials. Requirements for certification of officials are governed by the USTA Officiating Certification Regulations. The USTA Officials Committee adopts and amends these regulations in accordance with procedures determined and approved by the USTA Board. The USTA publishes these regulations at www.usta.com.

title: Officials certified
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.C. Certification of USTA Officials
text: Officials certified. The USTA shall certify categories of officials including, but not limited to, chair umpires, chief umpires, line umpires, referees, and roving umpires.

title: Procedure for Official to Appeal Certification Decisions
text:
Any member may file an appeal of a certification decision to the USTA Officials Committee if the USTA:
• Refuses to approve the member’s application or certification category; or
• Decertifies the official.

title: The USTA Officials Committee sets forth the process for appealing certification decisions
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.D. Procedure for Official to Appeal Certification Decisions
text: The USTA Officials Committee sets forth the process for appealing certification decisions. The process must be posted on the USTA’s website. Any changes to the process must be posted at least 90 days before becoming effective.

title: All appeals of a certification decision shall be submitted electronically to the USTA in a manner specified by the USTA Officials Committee
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.D. Procedure for Official to Appeal Certification Decisions
text: All appeals of a certification decision shall be submitted electronically to the USTA in a manner specified by the USTA Officials Committee. Absent good cause shown, any appeal not submitted within thirty (30) days of the date of the decision is barred.

title: Any person submitting an appeal of a certification decision shall be entitled to prompt written notification of all decisions
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.D. Procedure for Official to Appeal Certification Decisions
text: Any person submitting an appeal of a certification decision shall be entitled to prompt written notification of all decisions. Notification must be sent in accordance with the procedures established by the USTA Officials Committee.

title: Any member aggrieved by the decision of the USTA Officials Committee may file a grievance in accordance with USTA Bylaw 43
crumb: USTA Regulations · VII.D. Procedure for Official to Appeal Certification Decisions
text: Any member aggrieved by the decision of the USTA Officials Committee may file a grievance in accordance with USTA Bylaw 43.

title: Officiating Techniques and Procedures
text: In accordance with procedures determined and approved by the USTA Board, the Officiating Department, with the assistance of the USTA Officials Committee, shall establish procedures and techniques for officiating consistent with the ITF Rules of Tennis and the USTA regulations. The USTA shall publish these Officiating Techniques and Procedures at www.usta.com.

title: Court Monitors
text: Court Monitors are not USTA-certified officials. Under the guidance of the Referee, USTA-sanctioned tournaments are authorized to use Court Monitors. Court Monitors assume limited duties and responsibilities to ensure fair and sportsmanlike play in conformity with the USTA regulations, The Code, and the Rules of Tennis. All persons serving in the role of Court Monitor must comply and be current with the requirements of the USTA Safe Play Program (see usta.com/safeplay for more information). Further, all adult persons serving in the role of Court Monitor must be Safe Play Approved, including clearing a criminal background screen completing SafeSport training. Minors, aged 17 or younger, serving as Court Monitors, are not required to be Safe Play Approved and need to be supervised by an adult who (a) is Safe Play Approved and (b) maintains open and observable interactions with the minor Court Monitor at all times.

title: Junior Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII. General Ranking Regulations
text: Junior rankings are governed by the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations.

title: Adult and Family Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII. General Ranking Regulations
text:
Adult and Family rankings are governed by the USTA Adult and Family
Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations.

title: Wheelchair Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII. General Ranking Regulations
text:
Wheelchair rankings are governed by the USTA Wheelchair Tournament,
Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations.

title: Eligibility for Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII. General Ranking Regulations
text: Only the following categories of persons are eligible to receive a ranking:

title: U.S. Citizens
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII.D. Eligibility for Rankings
text: U.S. Citizens. Citizens of the United States.

title: Certain aliens
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII.D. Eligibility for Rankings
text:
Certain aliens.
• Permanent resident aliens. Permanent resident aliens of the United States.
• Diplomats. Aliens who have resided in the United States continuously for more than one year and who are members of families of persons in the diplomatic or consular corps.
• Aliens with Refugee Status. Aliens who have been granted Refugee Status.
• Aliens with Asylee Status. Aliens who have been granted Asylee Status.
• Aliens with Temporary Protected Status. Aliens who have been granted Temporary Protected Status.
• Aliens with Adjustment Status. Aliens whose I-485 (Application to Register Permanent Resident or Adjust Status) has been accepted for filing.
• British Columbians. Canadian citizens and landed Canadian immigrants who reside in British Columbia, provided that they were USTA members for at least one month during 2010 and so long as they do not allow their USTA memberships to lapse for a period of more than six months.

title: Documents commonly used to support a particular alien status include a permanent resident alien card (green card), Form I-94, or a receipt c
crumb: USTA Regulations · VIII.D. Eligibility for Rankings
text: FAC Comment VIII.D-1: Documents commonly used to support a particular alien status include a permanent resident alien card (green card), Form I-94, or a receipt confirming filing of the I-485.

title: National Junior Tournament Schedule
crumb: USTA Regulations · IX. Junior Tournaments and Rankings
text: Annually the USTA shall publish the National Junior Tournament Schedule, which shall include the USTA Junior National Championships and other tournaments authorized for sanction by the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation IX.E.). These two categories of tournaments are known collectively as the USTA Junior National Tournaments. The National Junior Tournament Schedule may also include ITF Junior tournaments.

title: Junior Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · IX. Junior Tournaments and Rankings
text: The USTA publishes rankings in the Junior Divisions authorized by the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation IX.E.). The USTA President may appoint a Coordinator of Junior Rankings to coordinate all rankings in these divisions.

title: Players eligible for Junior rankings and certain tournaments
text:
Players eligible for Junior rankings and certain tournaments. Players who hold a status listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D. are eligible:
• For a Junior ranking;
• To play in tournaments sanctioned by the USTA Junior Competition Committee (except tournaments that may specifically exempt players from these eligibility requirements); and
• To play in certain tournaments sanctioned by a Sectional Association listed in the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations.

title: Loss of eligibility
text:
Loss of eligibility. Players (including U.S. citizens) who have made a declaration of citizenship to a foreign country or who have accepted endorsement from another federation to an ITF international team competition shall lose eligibility, except that:
• Those players from British Columbia listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D.; and
• Players from Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Guam, and the Northern Mariana Islands may play if they meet the eligibility criteria of USTA Regulation VIII.D.

title: Reinstatement of eligibility
text:
Reinstatement of eligibility. A player who was previously eligible and lost eligibility by:
• Declaring citizenship to a foreign country or accepting endorsement from another federation to an ITF international team competition; or
• No longer being classified by the Department of Homeland Security as an alien with a status listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D. may apply for reinstatement. The Director of Player Development or the Director’s Designee, the Director of Junior Competition, the Chair of the USTA Junior Competition Committee, in consultation with the USTA General Counsel, shall rule on the request. The player may appeal the ruling to the USTA Board.

title: Sanctioning of USTA Junior National Tournaments
crumb: USTA Regulations · IX. Junior Tournaments and Rankings
text: The USTA Junior Competition Committee shall sanction all USTA Junior National Tournaments. The USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations govern the process by which these tournaments are sanctioned.

title: Authority for Committee to Adopt USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and
crumb: USTA Regulations · IX. Junior Tournaments and Rankings
text: Sanctioning Regulations Tournaments sanctioned by the USTA Junior Competition Committee, the process by which these tournaments are sanctioned, Junior rankings, and minimum requirements for tournaments sanctioned by the Sectional Associations and District Associations that count for Junior ranking are governed by the USTA Junior Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations as adopted and amended by a committee appointed by the USTA President and in accordance with procedures determined and approved by the USTA Board.

title: Eligibility for ITF International Team Competitions
crumb: USTA Regulations · IX. Junior Tournaments and Rankings
text: To be eligible to play on a U.S. international team, a player must meet all ITF eligibility requirements. Once a player has accepted a nomination for a non-U.S. international team, the player may not compete on a U.S. international team unless reinstated by the USTA under USTA Regulation IX.C.3. Reinstatement applies to U.S. citizens who reside in Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Guam, or the Northern Mariana Islands, and accept a nomination for their respective team.

title: To be endorsed by the USTA into ITF international team competition, ITF regulations require that a player be a citizen as evidenced by posse
crumb: USTA Regulations · IX.F. Eligibility for ITF International Team Competitions
text: FAC Comment IX.F-1: To be endorsed by the USTA into ITF international team competition, ITF regulations require that a player be a citizen as evidenced by possession of a valid U.S. passport, Certificate of Naturalization, or other documentation acceptable to the ITF. Additional ITF eligibility requirements apply. See the ITF Junior Circuit Regulations.

title: National Adult and Family Tournament Schedule
crumb: USTA Regulations · X. Adult and Family Tournaments and Rankings
text: Annually the USTA publishes the National Adult and Family Tournament Schedule, which will include the USTA Level 1 Adult and Family National Championships and other tournaments authorized for sanction by the USTA Adult and Family Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation X.E.). The National Adult and Family Tournament Schedule may also include ITF tournaments.

title: Adult and Family Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · X. Adult and Family Tournaments and Rankings
text: The USTA publishes rankings in the Adult and Family Divisions authorized by the USTA Adult and Family Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation X.E.).

title: Eligibility for Ranking
crumb: USTA Regulations · X. Adult and Family Tournaments and Rankings
text: Only the categories of persons listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D. are eligible to receive a ranking.

title: Sanctioning National Adult and Family Tournaments
crumb: USTA Regulations · X. Adult and Family Tournaments and Rankings
text: The USTA Adult Competition Committee sanctions all USTA Level 1 Adult and Family National Championships and other tournaments authorized by the USTA Adult and Family Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation X.E.). The USTA Adult and Family Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations govern the process by which these tournaments are sanctioned.

title: Authority for Committee to Adopt USTA Adult and Family Tournament,
crumb: USTA Regulations · X. Adult and Family Tournaments and Rankings
text:
Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations Tournaments sanctioned by the USTA Adult Competition Committee, the process by which these tournaments are sanctioned, Adult and Family rankings, and minimum requirements for tournaments sanctioned by the Sectional Associations and District Associations that count for ranking are governed by the USTA Adult and Family Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations as adopted and amended by a committee appointed by the USTA President and in accordance with procedures determined and approved by the USTA Board.
FAC Comment X-1: To be endorsed by the USTA into ITF international team competition, ITF regulations require that a player be a U.S. citizen as evidenced by possession of a valid U.S. passport, Certificate of Naturalization, or other documentation acceptable to the ITF. Additional ITF eligibility requirements may apply. See the ITF regulations. The USTA may apply for a waiver from the ITF Seniors Committee for players who do not meet this requirement. The waiver application must be received by the ITF Seniors Committee at least three months before the competition. U.S. citizens who reside in Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa, Guam, or the Northern Mariana Islands may play either for their respective team or the U.S. international team. A player who wants to be selected for the USTA team and is eligible to represent more than one country shall notify the USTA of these facts in sufficient time for the USTA to comply with requirement of notifying the ITF at least three months before the event.

title: Men’s Division
text: Eligible players under USTA Regulation XI.C. shall be ranked in the Professional Men’s singles and doubles divisions in the order in which their names appear on the ATP ranking list as of December 31.

title: Women’s Division
text: Eligible players under USTA Regulation XI.C. shall be ranked in the Professional Women’s singles and doubles divisions in the order in which their names appear on the WTA ranking list as of December 31.

title: Eligibility for Professional Ranking
text: Only the categories of persons listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D. are eligible to receive a professional ranking.

title: Review
text: Professional rankings are not subject to review or appeal.

title: Separating players from same school
crumb: USTA Regulations · XII.A. Method for Making Draw
text: Separating players from same school. When a scholastic or collegiate draw involves players from the same school, entries shall be placed in separate halves or quarters, as evenly as possible, depending upon the number of entries from that school.

title: Distribution of byes
crumb: USTA Regulations · XII.A. Method for Making Draw
text: Distribution of byes. Byes shall be distributed among the seeded players in the order of their seeding. If the number of byes exceeds the number of seeded players and if fewer than one player for each four lines on the draw sheet has been seeded, then the byes shall be placed as though one player for each four lines on the draw sheet had been seeded. Any remaining byes shall be placed as provided in the USTA Regulations.

title: Championship rounds
text:
Championship rounds.
a. Main draw. Two points for each match won.
b. Third-place playoff. One-half point for playoff for third and fourth place if feed-in is used through the quarterfinal round; but, no points for playoff for third and fourth place if feed-in through quarterfinals is not used.
c. Byes. If a player receives a bye in the first round, 4 points are given only if the second-round match is won.
d. Defaults. A default shall always be considered as a match won and points awarded accordingly.

title: Consolation rounds with feed-in through the quarters
text:
Consolation rounds with feed-in through the quarters.
a. Matches played. One point for each match won.
b. Byes. If player receives a first-round bye, one point is given if the second-round match is won.
c. Defaults. In all instances a default shall be considered as a match won and points awarded accordingly.

title: Consolation rounds with no feed-in through quarters
text: Consolation rounds with no feed-in through quarters. One-quarter point for loser of finals and one-half point for winner of finals.

title: Ties
text: Ties. In the event of a tie, co-titles shall be awarded.

title: Eligibility for Collegiate Ranking
crumb: USTA Regulations · XII. Collegiate and Scholastic Tournaments and Collegiate Rankings
text: Only the categories of persons listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D. are eligible to receive a collegiate ranking.

title: Collegiate Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · XII. Collegiate and Scholastic Tournaments and Collegiate Rankings
text:
Eligible players shall be ranked in the following Collegiate Men’s and Women’s singles and team doubles divisions in the order in which their names appear on the academic year-end ITA (Intercollegiate Tennis Association) ranking lists.
• Men’s and Women’s Collegiate – NCAA Division I
• Men’s and Women’s Collegiate – NCAA Division II
• Men’s and Women’s Collegiate – NCAA Division III
• Men’s and Women’s Collegiate – NAIA (National Association of Intercollegiate Athletics)
• Men’s and Women’s Collegiate – NJCAA (National Junior College Athletic Association) The Collegiate ranking period shall be June 1 to May 31. Results from the following NCAA Division I National Tournaments shall
be considered in both the Men’s and Women’s Collegiate—NCAA Division I ranking categories and the Top 500 ranking categories.
• ITA All-American Championships
• ITA National Indoor Championships
• NCAA Division I National Championships Collegiate rankings are not subject to review or appeal.

title: National Wheelchair Tournament Schedule
crumb: USTA Regulations · XIII. Wheelchair Tournaments and Rankings
text: Annually the USTA shall publish the National Wheelchair Tournament Schedule, which will include the USTA Level 1 Wheelchair National Championships and such other tournaments authorized for sanction by the USTA Wheelchair Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation XIII.E.). The National Wheelchair Tournament Schedule may also include ITF Wheelchair tournaments.

title: Wheelchair Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · XIII. Wheelchair Tournaments and Rankings
text: The USTA publishes rankings in the Wheelchair Divisions authorized by the USTA Wheelchair Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation XIII.E.).

title: Eligibility for Rankings
crumb: USTA Regulations · XIII. Wheelchair Tournaments and Rankings
text: In the Wheelchair Divisions, only the categories of persons listed in USTA Regulation VIII.D. are eligible to receive a ranking.

title: Sanctioning of National Wheelchair Tournaments
crumb: USTA Regulations · XIII. Wheelchair Tournaments and Rankings
text: The USTA Wheelchair Tennis Committee shall sanction all USTA Level 1 Wheelchair National Championships and other tournaments authorized by the USTA Wheelchair Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations (see USTA Regulation XIII.E.). The USTA Wheelchair Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations govern the process by which these tournaments are sanctioned.

title: Authority for Committee to Adopt USTA Wheelchair Tournament, Ranking,
crumb: USTA Regulations · XIII. Wheelchair Tournaments and Rankings
text: and Sanctioning Regulations Tournaments sanctioned by the USTA Wheelchair Tennis Committee, the process by which these tournaments are sanctioned, Wheelchair rankings, and minimum requirements for tournaments sanctioned by the Sectional Associations and District Associations that count for ranking are governed by the USTA Wheelchair Tournament, Ranking, and Sanctioning Regulations as adopted and amended by a committee appointed by the USTA President and in accordance with procedures determined and approved by the USTA Board.

title: Para-standing Tennis
text: Para-Standing Tennis is for individuals with physical disabilities who can play standing without using a wheelchair. Para-Standing Tennis is played on a 78foot court using Yellow Ball Tennis. It can also be played on a 78-foot court using Green Ball Tennis, on a 60-foot court using Orange Ball Tennis, and on a 36-foot court using Red Ball Tennis.

title: Eligible impairment
text: Eligible impairment. The criteria for eligibility to enter Para-Standing Tennis tournaments shall be published in Table 18.

title: Para-Standing Tennis Eligibility Classifications
text: Para-Standing Tennis Eligibility Classifications A player, if otherwise eligible, may enter any Para-Standing Division if the player has an eligible impairment that falls into one of four classifications described below as PST1, PST2, PST3 and PST4. Bounces Para- Bounces Bounces Permitted vs. Standing Permitted Permitted vs. a Wheelchair Impairment Tennis (PST) in PST an Able-Bodied Tennis Player in Classification Tournaments Player Non-Wheelchair Event Unilateral upper limb amputee PST1 One One One or similar impairment. Unilateral below-knee amputee, mild cerebral PST2 One Two One palsy, or other impairment with similar mobility level. Above-knee or bilateral belowknee amputee, bilateral arm PST3 Two Two Two impairment, or moderate to severe cerebral palsy. Short stature or other impairment PST4 Two Two Two with similar impact on mobility.

title: The International Para-Standing Tennis and Padel Association uses a more detailed system of classifications based on the International Paral
text:
FAC Comment XIV.A-1: The International Para-Standing Tennis and Padel Association uses a more detailed system of classifications based on the International Paralympic Committee’s eligible disability guidelines. These more detailed classification guidelines may be required for determining eligibility if a
Para-Standing Tournament is supported or sanctioned by the ITF. The system of classifying PST players by the International Para-Standing Tennis and Padel Association and the International Paralympic Committee is subject to review and development based on academic research and the sport’s evolving needs. Any changes to the PST classification system may result in an update to this table.

title: Junior Divisions
text:
Junior Divisions.
a. Age eligibility. A player, if otherwise eligible, may enter any Junior Para-Standing Division if the player has not exceeded the maximum age by the last day of the month during which the division is scheduled to start (see Table 4).
b. Net Generation PlayTracker Does Not Apply. The Net Generation PlayTracker sets the requirements to be met by a player under the age of 11 to compete in Junior Circuit Events and junior ranking tournaments that use a yellow ball. These requirements do not apply to participation in the Para-Standing Tennis tournaments for junior players. However, if a junior Para-Standing Tennis player competes in a non-Para-Standing junior division, the requirements of the Net Generation PlayTracker apply.

title: Wheelchair Divisions
text: Wheelchair Divisions. A player, if otherwise eligible, who meets a Para-Standing Tennis eligibility requirement may enter any Wheelchair Division if the player meets the eligibility requirements of that division (see USTA Regulation I.G.3.d.i. and ii. for eligibility information).

title: Adult and Family Divisions
text: Adult and Family Divisions. A player, if otherwise eligible, may enter any Adult or Family Division if the player meets the eligibility requirements of that division (see USTA Regulation I.G.3.a.-c. for eligibility information).

title: Two-Bounce Rule
text: The USTA determines the number of bounces of the ball permitted for Para- Standing Tennis players based on their eligibility classifications and will publish the number of bounces permitted in Table 18. When a Para-Standing Tennis player is permitted two bounces, the player must return the ball before it bounces a third time. The second bounce can be either in or out of the court boundaries. When a Para-Standing Tennis player who is permitted two bounces is playing with or against a person permitted only one bounce by Table 18 or the ITF Rules of Tennis, such Para-Standing Tennis Player is allowed two bounces while the other players are allowed only one bounce.

title: Mobility Devices
text: Any mobility device, such as a prosthetic, crutch, or orthotics, is considered part of the body, and all applicable rules that apply to a player’s body, shall apply to the mobility device.

title: Scheduling guidelines for maximum number of matches in a day
text: Scheduling guidelines for maximum number of matches in a day. The Referee shall comply, when reasonable, with the scheduling guidelines in Table 19.

title: Rest between matches
text: Rest between matches. The Referee shall offer players competing in Para-Standing Tennis tournaments at least the minimum rest between matches specified in Table 19.

title: Rest between sets
text: Rest between sets. The Referee shall offer players competing in Para- Standing Tennis tournaments at least the minimum rest between sets specified in Table 19.
